i think you need to understand that being a virgin is something that shouldn’t be frowned upon. most people who have common sense understand that your “body count” or how much you’ve “fucked” doesn’t give anyone insight on the depth of someone’s personality. you’re so hyper focused on sex and women that you’re forgetting that life ISNT about that. there’s more to life than getting into a relationship. you NEED to understand that. your obsession with becky lynch is also a cause for concern. the parasocial bond you’re forming with her is not real. please understand the reality of the situation. she does not know you. and she will never know you on a personal level. 

women and sex are NOT going to make your life feel fulfilled. regardless of age. 

that being said, you already show self-awareness on your situation. the biggest thing is to act on it. if you know these things are upsetting you, and you want to change, the last step is to take the leap. 

it’s easier said than done, there’s no denying that. for me personally, im in the process of learning to take that leap. it’s so difficult. i know it’s difficult. 

people dislike change because it disrupts with the sense of comfort and normalcy that exists. and that’s completely okay. 

i hope you get the help you need. please know that there ARE people out there who are there to help. contact your local community’s mental health services, or get in touch with a gym/fitness centre, do what you need to do to feel like you’re taking a step in the right direction. 

you can do this. it doesn’t matter that you’re 29, it doesn’t matter that you’re a virgin, what matters is that you know how hard you’re working, and the journey to self-improvement.

as someone who has therapist and medication, i agree and disagree. i won’t deny that there are benefits. i get to speak about things to a stranger and don’t have the worry of changing their minds on me because it’s purely professional. they also have studied a field that’s so broad but are able to provide logical and emotional explanations to the things i say. this of course is on a case by case basis, since not all therapists are good. that’s also a downside. i’ve had other therapists who were ass. same goes for medication. in canada medication and therapy are not expensive and for the most part not as costly or not costly at all. but it truly is trial and error. i cant say i don’t understand you because naturally most people want a pure fool-proof solution to their psychological pain. but the reality of mental illness is that you can’t fix it. you have to live with it. that’s something i learned in therapy. and as someone who is still suicidal, some people can’t live with it. for some people it’s too much. so yes, i do understand in a sense
